executive_summary.result: High Country Outfitters has a functioning outdoor retail ecommerce discovery foundation with rendered search result pages, broad browse navigation, robust filters, store-location inventory filters, active merchandising, cart functionality, and public policy/support paths. The corrected rendered-search capture recovered all tested commercial product/category, rental, local-team, and typo terms, and the public autocomplete API returned camp suggestions matching the user-observed visible dropdown. The added apparel-domain IR concept set scored 99/100 for rendered search and 85/100 for autocomplete across normalization, tokenization, synonyms, field weighting, query expansion, and document enrichment examples. The largest remaining risks are full visible autocomplete QA across the protected set, filter complexity, incomplete local/trust evidence from static crawl limits, and unavailable automated competitor benchmark evidence.

search.rationale: 9/9 product or collection queries returned fetch, rendered-search, or suggest evidence; typo recovery for patgonia was present; kayak-rental recovery was present.

autocomplete.rationale: 10/13 autocomplete/suggest probes returned product, collection, query, or page suggestions through the Shopify suggest endpoint; the camp follow-up API matched the user-observed visible dropdown. Rendered search input was available for 2/2 earlier probes.

browse.rationale: 12/14 API-sampled browse collections returned product samples, and 3/3 rendered collection pages exposed product links; navigation exposes gear, apparel, footwear, locations, rentals, brands, and sale paths.

filters.rationale: Rendered camping collection exposed 9 filter groups, including store-location inventory filters.

recommendations.rationale: Homepage and collection pages expose sale, staff-pick, new-arrival, and quick-add merchandising. Product recommendation depth was sampled but not exhaustively validated.

mobile_experience.rationale: Mobile rendered homepage exposed search=true and cart=true with store-pickup/free-shipping messaging, but checkout completion was not attempted.

product_discovery_overall.rationale: Average of search, autocomplete, browse, filters, recommendations/merchandising, and mobile evidence scores for this bounded public assessment.

ir_concept_tests.scope: Apparel-domain information-retrieval concept tests requested for the High Country Outfitters report.
ir_concept_tests.scoring_note: Scores are bounded public-evidence judgments from rendered search pages and browser-context Shopify suggest API responses. They are diagnostic IR concept scores, not replacements for the main report scorecard.

evidence: Rendered collection pages with products: Camping (16 visible product links); Paddlesports (6 visible product links); Patagonia (16 visible product links).

API-sampled browse collections with products: gear (24 sampled); camping (24 sampled); paddlesports (6 sampled); ski-gear (24 sampled); yeti-coolers (8 sampled); footwear (24 sampled); mens-clothing (24 sampled); womens-clothing (24 sampled); kids-apparel (22 sampled); accessories (24 sampled); patagonia (24 sampled); sale (24 sampled).
findings.customer_impact: Customers who browse by activity or department can find meaningful paths without starting from search.
findings.business_impact: The category architecture supports discovery and can absorb paid, email, and local-store traffic better than a search-only catalog.
findings.recommendation: Preserve browse/category depth, then test priority shopping journeys such as rain jacket, HOKA shoe, YETI cooler, kayak rental, and Atlanta Braves gift across desktop and mobile.

findings.observation: Rendered collection pages expose robust filters, including product type, vendor, size, price, availability, color, and store-location inventory.
evidence: Observed filter groups on camping collection: filter.v.t.shopify.target-gender, filter.p.product_type, filter.v.m.locationInventory.locations, filter.p.vendor, filter.v.option.size, filter.v.price.gte, filter.v.price.lte, filter.v.availability, filter.v.t.shopify.color-pattern.
Location inventory filters include Alpharetta - The Avalon, Athens - Downtown, Buckhead - Flagship Store, East Cobb - The Avenue.
findings.customer_impact: Customers can narrow by brand, size, price, availability, and pickup location, which is especially valuable for a regional retailer with multiple stores.
findings.business_impact: Store-level inventory filtering is a differentiator versus generic ecommerce pages, but long filter panels can become hard to scan without curation.
findings.recommendation: Keep location inventory prominent and consider prioritizing the highest-use filters above long vendor or size lists on mobile.

findings.observation: Homepage and collection evidence show active merchandising, sale framing, staff picks, quick-add controls, free-shipping threshold messaging, pickup messaging, and cart functionality.
evidence: Cart check added Camino 35 Carryall 2.0 Tote Bag and cart.js reported 1 item(s).
Homepage checks: sale=true, staff_pick=true, pickup=true, shipping=true.

Rendered support checks: Contact Us (phone, shipping, returns, store_locations, contact_form); Shipping And Return Policy (email, shipping, returns, contact_form); Locations (phone, shipping, returns, store_locations, contact_form).
findings.customer_impact: Shoppers can move from discovery to cart and see shipping or pickup cues before checkout.
findings.business_impact: The site has operational ecommerce foundations, so product-discovery improvements can plausibly connect to conversion rather than only awareness.
findings.recommendation: Validate quick-add and variant selection paths for top products, then test checkout entry, pickup selection, shipping thresholds, and return messaging before client-ready conclusions.

findings.category: Local Trust And Public Site Signals
findings.observation: The upstream local-site assessment is useful only as partial public-site evidence; its static crawl missed dynamic ecommerce paths and selected an invalid Pest Control demand/competitor layer.
evidence: Allowed upstream evidence: Local Visibility scored 20/100; Lead Conversion scored 0/100; Trust Signals scored 14/100; Message Clarity scored 25/100; Mobile Experience scored 33/100; AI Discoverability scored 0/100; Performance unavailable; Security & Reliability scored 83/100.

Excluded upstream sections: Generated sector was Pest Control and is invalid for outdoor retail ecommerce market evidence.; Generated competitor comparison used Pest Control queries and Pest Control competitors, so it is excluded from ecommerce market evidence..
findings.customer_impact: Static crawl limitations could understate live ecommerce features, while still flagging crawlability, local visibility, trust, and public-site evidence limits.
findings.business_impact: Combined reporting must separate what the ecommerce workflow directly observed from what the local website crawler inferred from one truncated page.
findings.recommendation: Use the local assessment as context, not market evidence, and rerun public-site/local evidence with a JavaScript-aware crawl if local SEO or store-lead conclusions become client-facing.

findings.observation: Outdoor-retail benchmark pages were attempted, but bounded public fetches were blocked or too low-signal for comparative market claims.
evidence: Unavailable or low-signal benchmark pages: REI (Public search page was not usable in this run: 403.); Backcountry (Public fetch returned status 202, but extracted text did not contain expected product-discovery benchmark signals.); Public Lands (Public search page was not usable in this run: 403.).
findings.customer_impact: Benchmark expectations for advice, reviews, events, and deep category education should be validated manually before being presented as competitor proof.
findings.business_impact: High Country can still lean into local inventory and store pickup, but this automated benchmark run should be treated as an evidence limit.
findings.recommendation: Run a browser-based/manual benchmark pass against REI, Backcountry, and Public Lands before making comparative claims; keep this automated result as a blocker note.

evidence_limits: This is a bounded public-site assessment run from 2026-07-02, not a full analytics, revenue, customer, or platform-admin audit.
Checkout was not completed; cart entry was tested only through a public Shopify cart session.

Search and autocomplete evidence uses sampled queries, not every query or every public collection node. Camp autocomplete suggestions are public-API backed and user-observed in the UI, but full visible dropdown QA across every protected term was not run.
The apparel-domain IR concept scores are diagnostic examples, not a complete apparel relevance benchmark or a replacement for analytics, conversion, or full catalog parity testing.
Product inventory, prices, promotions, and availability can change after capture.

Several plain fetch endpoints returned access-verification pages in the final run; rendered browser evidence is used where available, and unrendered blocked queries are treated as unverified, not definitive zero-result evidence.
The upstream local website assessment crawled one meaningful page and truncated the homepage response at its configured size limit.
The upstream Pest Control demand fit and Pest Control competitor comparison were excluded from ecommerce market evidence.
Outdoor-retail competitor/benchmark pages were attempted, but automated public fetches were blocked or low-signal, so this report does not make competitor market claims.
exact_next_action: Review the complete Northvalley PDF report and decide whether to use it as the review draft or first broaden ecommerce validation with all-node browse/search parity, full protected-set autocomplete/mobile journey QA, browser/manual competitor benchmark, checkout/pickup policy review, and a larger apparel IR relevance set.
